question_text: Figure 6.20 shows a metal rod PQ resting on the smooth rails AB and positioned between the poles of a permanent magnet. The rails, the rod, and the magnetic field are in three mutual perpendicular directions. A galvanometer G connects the rails through a switch K. Length of the rod = 15 cm, B = 0.50 T, resistance of the closed loop containing the rod = 9.0 mΩ. Assume the field to be uniform. Suppose K is open and the rod is moved with a speed of 12 cm s−1 in the direction shown. Give the polarity and magnitude of the induced emf. Is there an excess charge built up at the ends of the rods when K is open? What if K is closed? With K open and the rod moving uniformly, there is no net force on the electrons in the rod PQ even though they do experience magnetic force due to the motion of the rod. Explain. What is the retarding force on the rod when K is closed? How much power is required (by an external agent) to keep the rod moving at the same speed (=12 cm s−1) when K is closed? How much power is required when K is open? How much power is dissipated as heat in the closed circuit? What is the source of this power?

parts.part_text: Give the polarity and magnitude of the induced emf.
parts.answer_text: Induced emf = 9 mV; polarity of the induced emf is such that end P shows positive while end Q shows negative.

steps.description: Identify the parameters: length of the rod, magnetic field strength, and speed.
Calculate the induced emf using the formula e = Bvl.

parts.final_answer: Therefore, the induced emf is 9 mV with end P positive and end Q negative.

parts.part_text: Is there an excess charge built up at the ends of the rods when K is open? What if K is closed?
parts.answer_text: Yes; when key K is closed, excess charge is maintained by the continuous flow of current. When key K is open, there is excess charge built up at both ends of the rods.
parts.final_answer: Excess charge is built up at both ends when K is open.

parts.part_text: Explain why there is no net force on the electrons in the rod PQ when K is open.
parts.answer_text: There is no net force on the electrons in rod PQ when key K is open and the rod is moving uniformly because the magnetic force is cancelled by the electric force set-up due to the excess charge of opposite nature at both ends of the rods.
parts.final_answer: Thus, the forces balance out, resulting in no net force on the electrons.

parts.part_text: What is the retarding force on the rod when K is closed?
parts.answer_text: Retarding force exerted on the rod, F = IBl.
parts.final_answer: The retarding force is given by the product of current, magnetic field strength, and length of the rod.

parts.part_text: How much power is required (by an external agent) to keep the rod moving at the same speed (=12 cm s−1) when K is closed? How much power is required when K is open?
parts.answer_text: When key K is open, no power is expended. When key K is closed, power is provided by an external agent.
parts.final_answer: Power is required when K is closed, but none when K is open.

parts.part_text: How much power is dissipated as heat in the closed circuit?
parts.answer_text: Power dissipated as heat = I²R = (1)² × 9 × 10−3 = 9 mW.

steps.description: Calculate power dissipated using the formula P = I²R.

parts.final_answer: The power dissipated as heat in the closed circuit is 9 mW.

parts.part_text: What is the source of this power?
parts.answer_text: The source of this power is an external agent.
parts.final_answer: Power is supplied by an external agent.
